title: The record that refused to die
text: {{1}} was streaming that was supposed to kill the LP, {{2}} sales of vinyl have risen every year {{3}} 2006. What matters is not only the sound, which many listeners honestly cannot distinguish from a good digital copy, {{4}} the object: a large sleeve worth framing, a ritual of sliding the disc out and dropping the needle, and music {{5}} stops when the side ends. Buying a record is a small ceremony, {{6}} begins with browsing and ends with cleaning the grooves, and the ceremony itself appears to be the product. {{7}} same slowness that once made vinyl obsolete now makes it precious: in an age of infinite, instant playlists, the record player offers a rare, deliberate way of listening to an album {{8}} a whole.

gaps.hint: cleft pronoun: ___ was streaming that was supposed

gaps.explanation: Contrast between prediction and reality: but.

gaps.hint: conjunction: not only the sound, ___ the object
relative: music ___ stops when the side ends
gaps.explanation: Defining relative after 'music' as the subject; no comma, so 'that' heads it.

gaps.hint: relative: a ceremony, ___ begins with browsing
gaps.explanation: Non-defining relative after the comma referring to the ceremony.
'The same' is the fixed definite phrase.
'As a whole' — the fixed phrase meaning 'in its entirety'.
